subject.title: fix(llm): summarize ephemeral tool results to preserve prefix cache

question: What model-visible tool-result policy should OpenClaw use for prefix-matching cache providers in this bug: heartbeat/status-only placeholders, a provider-specific cache strategy, or broad placeholders for core tools such as `exec` and `read`?
rationale: The technically easy change alters what future model turns can see from prior tool execution, so correctness depends on maintainer intent rather than a purely mechanical code repair.

options.title: Narrow to low-information tools
options.body: Keep command, file, web, and memory results visible by default, and only summarize maintainer-approved heartbeat/status outputs after rebase and live DeepSeek proof.

options.title: Adopt broad placeholders deliberately
options.body: Allow broad fixed placeholders for selected core tools, but require explicit maintainer ownership, tests for changed reasoning behavior, docs, and live cache proof before merge.

options.title: Defer to provider/cache work
options.body: Pause or close this branch if the desired fix is the provider-specific cache-boundary path tracked by adjacent DeepSeek cache PRs instead of hiding tool results.

recommendation.title: Narrow to low-information tools
recommendation.body: Keep command, file, web, and memory results visible by default, and only summarize maintainer-approved heartbeat/status outputs after rebase and live DeepSeek proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the recent `packages/ai` provider extraction and is the best current routing candidate for deciding where provider-level cache behavior should live.
